pr_title: shared: highlight directives when dumping configs
pr_body:
We already highlight sections and "de-highlight" comments, so let's add the last piece of the puzzle and highlight the configuration directives to visually distinguish them from the values.

Closes: #13416

---

Example:

![Screenshot_20231207_105604](https://github.com/systemd/systemd/assets/679338/202c0531-2a0c-4b9f-a071-4350128b708e)
pr_comments:
Updated as requested. Also, I limited the highlighting only when `CAT_FORMAT_HAS_SECTIONS` is specified, since the highlighting makes sense only for the "ini" format, not for the sysusers/tmpfiles/etc. formats.

While testing this I noticed that `systemd-analyze cat-config` doesn't highlight sections, since its call site was missing the `CAT_FORMAT_HAS_SECTIONS`, so I updated that as well.

issue_context.title: Add syntax highlighting to "systemctl cat"
issue_context.body:
When I run

systemctl cat systemd-sysctl.service

--> there is no output color

I want display output color same as vim editor

vim /lib/systemd/system/systemd-sysctl.service

Thanks
comments: you mean, as in syntax highlighting? hmm, uh. maybe using `bat` is what you want? i.e. PAGER=bat? it currently doesn't have syntax highlighting for systemd unit files, but sounds like something they might be interested in to add?

yes, it will more easier to see

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10233106/63906084-9b13e200-ca40-11e9-94ea-4fdc0356cc8d.png)

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10233106/63906096-abc45800-ca40-11e9-9574-d17e1361913e.png)

review_comments: I do not think it is necessary to built a string. How about to directly print the line in this case ?
That would mean splitting the final `printf()` below and then tracking if we printed the highlighted string or not (IIUC), wouldn't that make the code/logic harder to follow?
Yeah, I prefer that. But that's a kind of optimization, and this logic is not performance sensitive. If you do not like that, let's go with the current form. Merging.
